properties.name: The acting-agent stamp (#632) reaches AUTHORED_BY edges only; a "who" held as a node property (Question.answered_by, idea 2) gets the agent only if its writer reads acting() itself
properties.statement: MEASURED 2026-09-29 while building idea 2 (cap:a-question-names-whom-it-was-put-to-and-who-answered) on top of #632. The ACTS_FOR rung stamps `*_via` in exactly one place, the store's edge write, and only when the edge type is AUTHORED_BY (crates/reflow2-core/src/acting.rs stamp_through_acting_agent: `if edge_type != edge::AUTHORED_BY { return Ok(None) }`). So "every write records the agent" holds for every authorship, review and approval, and for nothing else that names a person. Idea 2 records whom a question was put to and who answered it as Question PROPERTIES (asked_of, answered_by), because neither is authorship: an AUTHORED_BY role on the Question would say the answerer made the question, and an approver role on an asked Question already means "assigned, not yet given", which makes a different addressee and answerer ambiguous. The expected "answers carry the acting agent automatically" therefore did NOT hold: the branch added Question.answered_via, written by answer_question from DesignGraph::acting(), with ACTS_FOR drawn to the answerer through the same record_acts_for. The class: any future "who" that is not an AUTHORED_BY role (an addressee, a claimant, an owner set by a property) needs its writer to read acting() or it records no agent. NOT ESTABLISHED: whether OWNED_BY and CLAIMS writes should be stamped too; that is intent.
